These are widely-documented, publicly-known facts about how digital Plinko titles work (peg-board drop games popularised by online casino/crypto-casino software studios). No specific provider's RTP, house edge or paytable is claimed here - those figures vary by studio and must come from that studio's own published game rules, never guessed.

howItWorks.summary: A ball is dropped from the top of a triangular field of pegs and bounces left or right at each peg row before landing in one of several multiplier slots along the bottom.
steps: The player sets a stake and, in most implementations, a risk level (commonly Low, Medium or High) and a row count (commonly 8-16 rows).
Pressing play/drop triggers a Random Number Generator (RNG) that determines the ball's left/right bounce at every peg.
The ball settles in one of the bottom slots; each slot has a fixed multiplier that is applied to the stake.
Higher risk settings and edge slots typically carry higher multipliers and lower landing probability; centre slots typically carry lower multipliers and higher landing probability.

riskLevels.description: Narrower spread of multipliers, more landings near the centre, smaller swings round to round.
A middle ground between Low and High - moderate multiplier spread.
Widest multiplier spread; edge slots can pay significantly more, but most drops land closer to the centre for a smaller return.

fairnessConcepts.rng: Licensed real-money Plinko titles use a certified Random Number Generator, independently tested by labs such as GLI, eCOGRA or iTech Labs.
fairnessConcepts.provablyFair: Crypto-funded Plinko variants often additionally publish a 'provably fair' scheme: a server seed (hashed and shown before play) and a client seed are combined to produce each outcome, so a player can independently verify after the fact that the result wasn't altered.
fairnessConcepts.houseEdge: Every Plinko paytable is built with a house edge (the average multiplier across all slots, weighted by landing probability, is below 1x). The exact edge is set by the game studio and disclosed in that game's information/paytable screen - always check the specific title's own rules rather than relying on general figures.

demoVsRealMoney.demo: A demo/free-play mode uses virtual credits with no real value and no withdrawal - it exists to let players learn the board and risk settings before ever depositing.
demoVsRealMoney.realMoney: Real-money play is only available through operators holding a valid licence in the player's jurisdiction. In Great Britain that means a current Gambling Commission (UKGC) licence; players should verify a licence number via the public register before depositing.
